questions.source_label: Chapter 11.2 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q3
questions.text: A point $P$ lies on the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$. If the distance from $P$ to the origin is exactly $4$, what is the product of the distances from $P$ to the two foci of the ellipse?

questions.source_label: Chapter 11.3 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q5
questions.text: A hyperbola centered at the origin has its foci on the $x$-axis. Its asymptotes intersect at the origin to form an angle of $60^\circ$ that contains the transverse axis. If the distance between the two vertices is 12, find the distance between the two foci.

Determine all real values of \(k\) for which
\[
x^2-4x+y^2+2ky+4k-5=0
\]
represents exactly one point.
